newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Canada firm signs $20 mln Tanzania oil search deal.
newsitem.headline: Canada firm signs $20 mln Tanzania oil search deal.

text.p: Canadian oil firm Canop International has signed a $20 million oil exploration deal with Tanzania, Canadian officials said on Wednesday.

Canadian High Commissioner (ambassador) to Tanzania, Verona Edelstein, told Reuters the deal was signed on Tuesday by Canop chairman and former Canadian prime minister Joe Clark and Tanzania Energy and Minerals Minister Abdallah Kigoda.
The agreement brings to four the number of Canadian petroleum exploration companies operating in the east African country.

"Canop, along with three other Canadian petroleum exploration companies intend to invest a total of some $100 million in exploring for oil and gas in Tanzania within the next year or two," said Edelstein.
"They believe the prospects for success over time are strong."
Clark said Canop's exploration programme would include reprocessing of seismic data as well as drilling several exploration wells.
The deal known as the Production Sharing Agreement (PSA) covers the Dar es Salaam platform situated onshore between the mouth of the Ruvu river to the north and the Rufiji delta to the south.
The exploration zone also includes the Mafia basin which lies on the broad continental shelf and islands east of the Rufiji delta and north of the Songo Songo shelf.
Canop International was established in early 1996 by Clark and another principal, Alan Smith, with a mandate to pursue oil and gas exploration opportunities outside Canada.
Other Canadian companies in Tanzania are Dublin International Petroleum, a subsidiary of Tanganyika Oil of Vancouver, and Antrim Resources and Ocelot Energy Inc, both from Calgary.

Investment in Tanzania's fledgling mineral sector grew from $15.8 million in 1987 to more than $53 million in 1992, about two percent of gross domestic product (GDP). The government aims to raise this level to 10 percent by the year 2025.
